program_name: CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF, READ THIS FIRST. The brief assumes the English-taught curriculum is itself called "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment". It is not. "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment" is merely the official ENGLISH RENDERING of the whole Italian-titled degree "Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente" (acronym IMEA). The English-taught curriculum INSIDE that degree has its own name: "Sustainable Energy" (Italian: "Energia Sostenibile"), acronym SE, curriculum no. 4 of 4. Anyone applying must ask for the SUSTAINABLE ENERGY curriculum by name; asking for "the English programme in Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment" will not identify a distinct course. THE DIPLOMA. The degree awarded is "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente", degree class LM-33. The Italian degree title is what appears on the diploma; the curriculum name (Sustainable Energy) does NOT change the diploma title and is not part of the qualification's legal name. Art. 1 of the binding Didactic Regulations states it directly: "Il presente Regolamento disciplina gli aspetti organizzativi del Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente (classe LM-33). Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente (Mechanical Engineering for Energy and Environment, in Inglese) afferisce al Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale, e tenuto in lingua Italiana ed Inglese ed e erogato in modalita convenzionale." NOTE THE OFFICIAL ENGLISH NAME IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS UNINA PAGES: the orientation portal and the international course catalogue write "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment" (with "the"); the Didactic Regulations and the departmental site write "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and Environment" (without "the"); the a.y. 2026/2027 Annex 1 cover writes "MECHANICAL ENGINEERING FOR THE ENERGY AND THE ENVIRONMENT". All three refer to the same degree. ADMINISTERING STRUCTURES. Department: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale (DII, Department of Industrial Engineering, https://www.dii.unina.it). School/Faculty: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School, SPSB). Teaching area recorded centrally: "Ingegneria". Duration: 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS, conventional (in-person) delivery mode. THE FOUR CURRICULA ("percorsi formativi" / "curricular paths" of automatic approval, chosen when the Study Plan is submitted): (1) Sistemi Energetici Innovativi / Innovative Energy Systems (SEI) - Italian; (2) Gestione Avanzata dell'Energia / Advanced Energy Management (GAE) - Italian; (3) Sistemi Propulsivi / Propulsion Systems (SP) - Italian; (4) Sustainable Energy / Energia Sostenibile (SE) - ENGLISH. A fifth optional overlay, the Minor in Green Technologies (MGT), is Italian/English. IMPORTANT: the English names of the three ITALIAN-taught curricula are also English words ("Innovative Energy Systems", "Advanced Energy Management", "Propulsion Systems"). Do not be misled by the English-looking names - only SUSTAINABLE ENERGY is taught in English. MINOR IN GREEN TECHNOLOGIES (also branded "Minor in Ingegneria delle Transizioni in Tecnologie Green" / "Minor in Transition Engineering in Green Technologies"): an optional interdisciplinary 30-CFU overlay (15 curricular + 15 extra-curricular CFU, the extra-curricular ones obtainable within one additional year at no extra cost), certified by an Open Badge at https://bestr.it/badge/show/2728. DEGREE PROGRAMME DIRECTOR / COORDINATOR: Prof. Fabio Bozza (fabio.bozza@unina.it, tel. +39 081 7683274), named as "Degree Programme Director" on the orientation portal and as "Coordinatore Didattico" on the departmental "Referenti e Commissioni" page. level: MASTER - Italian "Laurea Magistrale" (second-cycle degree, EQF level 7), 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS. This CONFIRMS the "level: master" given in the research brief. The central unina.it course record states "Tipo di corso: Magistrale", "Durata: 2 anni", "Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 1 livello" (entry qualification: a first-cycle/bachelor degree). The orientation portal fact-sheet header states "Master's Degree" and "Degree required: Laurea I Livello". CREDIT VALUE OF EACH CFU: Art. 6 of the Didactic Regulations states "Ogni CFU corrisponde convenzionalmente a 25 ore di impegno formativo complessivo" - one CFU equals 25 hours of total student workload, so 120 CFU equals 3,000 nominal hours over two years. HOW THE 120 CFU ARE SPLIT IN THE ENGLISH-TAUGHT SUSTAINABLE ENERGY CURRICULUM (identical in the a.y. 2025/2026 and a.y. 2026/2027 study plans): Mandatory curricular courses (Table O4a) 18 CFU + mandatory curricular courses (Table O4b) 24 CFU + curricular courses of the student's choice (Tables B4 and C4) 12 + 12 = 24 CFU + related/supplementary activities of the student's choice (Table A4) 15 CFU + autonomous-choice activities (Table D4) 15 CFU + Additional Language Proficiency 3 CFU + Internship (tirocinio) 9 CFU + Final Exam (thesis) 12 CFU = 120 CFU. The orientation portal restates the same split as "Related/Supplementary Learning Activities, 15 credits; Mandatory Curricular Courses, 18 credits; Curricular Courses (mandatory or elective), 48 credits; Autonomously chosen Courses, 15 credits; Additional Language Skills/Additional Knowledge, 3 credits; Internship, 9 credits; Final Exam, 12 credits". PART-TIME OPTION EXISTS: the departmental site publishes a separate "Manifesto degli Studi Tempo Parziale" (part-time study plan) at https://meccanica.dii.unina.it/it/manifesto-lmea-tp. THESIS AND FINAL EXAM: 12 CFU, an academic commission evaluates a master's thesis of a theoretical, methodological, numerical or experimental nature; it may be carried out in companies or research bodies in Italy or abroad under a university supervisor; "The written report and discussion may be developed in English". Presentation lasts about 15 minutes. Graduation-session calendar: https://www.scuolapsb.unina.it/esame-di-laurea-collegio-degli-studi-di-ingegneria/. INTERNSHIP: 9 CFU, either extramoenia (in companies, public or private research centres) or intramoenia (in university laboratories); ALL students must complete workplace health-and-safety training plus medical checks before starting. CAREER/EMPLOYABILITY DATA PUBLISHED BY THE PROGRAMME: "According to Almalaurea 2021, 98% of IMEA graduates were employed within three years after the master's degree" (departmental orientation page, English version). The older 2020 brochure claimed "95% of people with a permanent position within three years after the degree, source Almalaurea database 2018". Treat both as programme self-reported marketing figures.
teaching_language: THE DEGREE AS A WHOLE IS BILINGUAL, NOT ENGLISH. The orientation-portal fact sheet records "Language: ENG/ITA"; the international course catalogue lists it as "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment ITA/ENG" (contrast the same catalogue's "- ENG" entries such as Data Science or Transportation Engineering and Mobility, which are fully English degrees). Art. 1 of the Didactic Regulations: the course "e tenuto in lingua Italiana ed Inglese" (is taught in Italian and English). ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR CURRICULA IS ENGLISH, AND IT IS FULLY ENGLISH. The binding table "PERCORSI FORMATIVI E LINGUA DI EROGAZIONE" / "CURRICULA AND LANGUAGES" in Annex 1 of the Didactic Regulations assigns: SEI = Italiano/Italian; GAE = Italiano/Italian; SP = Italiano/Italian; SE (Sustainable Energy / Energia Sostenibile) = Inglese/English; MGT (Minor in Green Technologies) = Italiano/Inglese / Italian/English. The Italian premise is explicit: the four standard paths are "'Sistemi Energetici Innovativi', 'Gestione Avanzata dell'Energia', 'Sistemi Propulsivi', e 'Sustainable Energy' (quest'ultimo integralmente erogato in lingua inglese)" - the last one delivered ENTIRELY in English. The English version of the same premise reads: four curricula "called 'Innovative Energy Systems', 'Advanced Energy Management', 'Propulsion Systems', held in Italian Language, and 'Sustainable Energy', held in English, made up of 120 CFU". Art. 2 adds that the offer is organised in several paths "uno dei quali, piu generalista, erogato integralmente in lingua inglese" - one of which, the more generalist one, is delivered entirely in English. THE RULE THAT DECIDES A COURSE'S LANGUAGE, verbatim from Annex 1: "Nelle tabelle delle attivita formative riportate nelle pagg. seguenti, gli insegnamenti con primo titolo in italiano sono erogati in italiano; gli insegnamenti con primo titolo in inglese sono erogati in inglese." (English version: "In the tables of educational activities on the following pages, courses with first title in Italian are offered in Italian language, while those with first title in English are offered in English.") In the Sustainable Energy tables EVERY course is listed English-title-first, so every course is delivered in English. THE COMPLETE ENGLISH-TAUGHT SUSTAINABLE ENERGY SYLLABUS (a.y. 2026/2027 Annex 1, identical to 2025/2026). Table O4a, mandatory, 18 CFU, TAF B: Heat Transfer Principles in Engineering (9 CFU, Yr1/Sem1, IIND-07/A); Principles and Applications of Fluid Machinery (9 CFU, Yr1/Sem2, IIND-06/A). Table O4b, mandatory, 24 CFU, TAF B: Advanced Energy Systems and Technologies - Fundamentals (6 CFU, Yr1/Sem1) and Applications (6 CFU, Yr1/Sem2), IIND-07/A; Advanced Powertrains for a Sustainable Mobility - Fundamentals (6 CFU, Yr2/Sem1) and Modeling and Optimization (6 CFU, Yr2/Sem2), IIND-06/A. Table B4, choose 12 CFU in Yr2, TAF B: Fuel Cells for Power Generation and Energy Storage (6); Gas Turbines for Sustainable Power Production (6); Low Carbon Boilers and Industrial Furnaces (6); Hydro, Wind and Ocean Energy Conversion Systems (6); Fluid Power Systems for Energy Sustainability of Off-Road Vehicles (6). Table C4, choose 12 CFU in Yr2, TAF B: Refrigeration and Heat Pump Technologies (6); Thermo-economic Optimization of Complex Energy Systems (6); Lighting Technology and Acoustics (6); Energy and Buildings (6); Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Systems (6). Table A4, choose 15 CFU, TAF C (related/supplementary, largely borrowed from other Federico II master's degrees): Energy Management for Transportation (9 CFU, from LM-TEAM); Electrical Technologies for the Ecological Transition, split into Electric Energy Storage (3) + Electric Mobility and Generation from Renewables (3), from LM-IELT; Smart, Resilient and Sustainable City (9 CFU, from LM-IAMT); Circular Bioeconomy for the Ecological Transition (6 CFU, from LM-IAMT); Sustainable Combustion Processes for Energy Conversion (9 CFU); Industrial Ecology and Green Engineering (6 CFU, from LM-ICHI). Table D4, autonomous choice, 15 CFU, TAF D: the entries are literally "6 CFUs English courses from every didactic regulation table" and "9 CFUs English courses from every didactic regulation table" (Italian: "Insegnamento in inglese da 6 CFU da qualsiasi Tabella del Manifesto") - i.e. even the free-choice credits must be taken from ENGLISH-taught courses. THIS IS THE KEY POINT: a Sustainable Energy student can complete all 120 CFU without a single Italian-taught examination. OTHER ENGLISH-TAUGHT COURSES AVAILABLE ACROSS THE PROGRAMME'S TABLES (course-description annex marks them "INGLESE"), useful for the free-choice credits: Advanced Energy Systems and Technologies; Advanced Powertrains for a Sustainable Mobility; Circular Bioeconomy for the Ecological Transition; Electric and Hybrid Vehicles; Electrical Technologies for the Ecological Transition; Energy and Buildings; Energy Sustainability in Smart Transportation; Fluid Power Systems for Energy Sustainability of Off-Road Vehicles; Fuel Cells for Power Generation and Energy Storage; Gas Turbines for Sustainable Power Production; Heat Transfer Principles in Engineering; Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning; Hydro, Wind and Ocean Energy Conversion; Lighting Technology and Acoustics; Low Carbon Boilers and Industrial Furnaces; Machine Learning and Big Data; Mathematical Models and Computational Methods for Engineering; Network Security; Principles and Applications of Fluid Machinery; Refrigeration and Heat Pump Technologies; Smart and Electric Mobility; Smart, Resilient and Sustainable City; Space Propulsion; Sustainable Combustion Processes for Energy Conversion; Sustainable Materials; Technologies for Information Systems; Thermo-economic Optimization of Complex Energy Systems; Thermo-mechanical Technologies for Energy. THESIS AND FINAL EXAM MAY BE IN ENGLISH: "La relazione scritta e la discussione potranno essere sviluppate in inglese". [uncertain] TWO PRACTICAL CAVEATS AN APPLICANT MUST WEIGH. (1) The curriculum is chosen at STUDY-PLAN submission (normally by 31 October of each academic year), NOT at admission, and it is a "piano di studi di automatica approvazione" declared to the Engineering Student Office - there is no separate English-track admission, no separate seat allocation and no guarantee published anywhere that the SE path runs with a minimum cohort. (2) University life outside the SE lecture theatre (student office, enrolment paperwork, the departmental Italian-language site, most notices, the Study Plan procedure page http://meccanica.dii.unina.it/it/piani-di-studio-lmea and the internship safety procedure) is conducted in Italian; the English-language departmental pages are partial mirrors. Federico II itself does NOT require Italian for English-taught programmes (international.unina.it: "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required"), but day-to-day administration in Naples effectively assumes it.

degree_class: LM-33 - Italian degree class LM-33 "Ingegneria meccanica" (Mechanical Engineering). This CONFIRMS the degree_class given in the research brief. Stated identically across four official sources: (a) the orientation-portal fact-sheet header, English version, "Degree class LM-33"; (b) the central unina.it course record, "Classe di Laurea: LM-33 Ingegneria meccanica"; (c) Art. 1 of the Didactic Regulations, "Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente (classe LM-33)"; (d) the cover of Annex 1 to the a.y. 2026/2027 Didactic Regulations, "MECHANICAL ENGINEERING FOR THE ENERGY AND THE ENVIRONMENT - CLASS LM-33". AlmaLaurea's transparency record also files the course as "Ingegneria meccanica per l'energia e l'ambiente (LM-33)" under codicione 0630107303400002. Teaching area (area didattica) recorded centrally as "Ingegneria"; School: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base; Department: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale. Administratively consistent: engineering class, engineering department, engineering student office at Piazzale Tecchio. NOTE FOR CREDENTIAL RECOGNITION: LM-33 is the same class as Federico II's sister degree "Ingegneria Meccanica per la Progettazione e la Produzione" (LM-IMPP), which shares the same admission test and the same School-level admission rules. The two are distinct degree programmes with distinct curricula - do not confuse the Sustainable Energy curriculum of LM-IMEA with the "Sustainable Development" curriculum of LM-IMPP.
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS WITH A COMPULSORY TWO-PART ADMISSION CHECK. The orientation-portal fact sheet labels it "Admission: Verifica di preparazione" (verification of preparation), NOT "Libero" and NOT "numero programmato". There is NO numerus clausus, NO ranked competitive selection, NO bando/call for applications, NO TOLC and NO application fee. POSITIVE PROOF THAT THERE IS NO SEAT CAP: the University's official index of programmed-number courses for a.y. 2026/2027 (https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/offerta-formativa/corsi-numero-programmato) lists only FIVE two-year master's degrees - Precision Livestock Farming (Zootecnica di Precisione), Professioni sanitarie, Psicologia Clinica e degli interventi nei contesti sociali e dello sviluppo, Scienze Enologiche and Scienze della Nutrizione Umana. Neither "Ingegneria meccanica per l'energia e l'ambiente" nor any mechanical/energy engineering course appears anywhere on that page. THE TWO GATES, both compulsory (Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations, applied uniformly across all master's degrees of the Collegio di Ingegneria of the SPSB). GATE 1 - POSSESSION OF THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (see academic_requirements). Verbatim: "La verifica della personale preparazione e obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari" - the personal-preparation check is compulsory in every case, and only students who already hold the curricular requirements may take it. "L'iscrizione al Corso di Laurea Magistrale non e consentita in difetto dei requisiti minimi curriculari" - enrolment is NOT permitted if the minimum curricular requirements are missing. In that case the CCD (Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico, the Teaching Coordination Committee) prescribes enrolment in single course units (Corsi Singoli, https://www.unina.it/-/5601348-iscrizione-ai-corsi-singoli) and passing their examinations BEFORE matriculation. GATE 2 - VERIFICATION OF THE ADEQUACY OF PERSONAL PREPARATION, which explicitly includes language competence: "A valle della verifica del possesso dei requisiti curriculari, e altresi obbligatoria la verifica dell'adeguatezza della personale preparazione dello studente, incluso il possesso di adeguate competenze linguistiche." This gate has an AUTOMATIC PASS at a CFU-weighted bachelor average of 24/30 or above, and an admission TEST for everyone below it (see entry_exam_or_test). A SOFT LANDING FOR PARTIALLY-QUALIFIED L-9 GRADUATES: "Studenti in possesso di Laurea L-9 o equipollente ma con meno di 18 CFU nei settori IIND-06/A, IIND-06/B e IIND-07/A, saranno ammessi al corso di Laurea Magistrale con raccomandazione di un Piano di Studi Individuale che prevede uno specifico percorso di allineamento, senza aggravio di CFU totali" - such students ARE admitted, with a recommended individual study plan containing an alignment path, at no extra CFU cost. The CCD may also recognise credit equivalences from other subject areas for the 18-CFU core requirement. THREE PRACTICAL ROUTES FOR AN APPLICANT. (1) ITALIAN-QUALIFICATION APPLICANTS: enrol online at https://www.segrepass.unina.it between 16 July and the ordinary deadline. (2) EU CITIZENS, AND ANYONE (EU or non-EU) LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU, HOLDING A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION: no competitive application and no Universitaly pre-enrolment. Per international.unina.it they "have unrestricted access to university courses if you hold a foreign qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification. In this case you have to send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements". For this degree the Coordinator is Prof. Fabio Bozza (fabio.bozza@unina.it); the named contacts for foreign-student enrolment are Prof. Francesco Pelella (francesco.pelella@unina.it) and Prof.ssa Enrica Malfi (enrica.malfi@unina.it), with Prof. Alfonso William Mauro (alfonsowilliam.mauro@unina.it) as international-students contact. (3) NON-EU APPLICANTS RESIDING ABROAD: compulsory pre-enrolment on the UNIVERSITALY portal (https://www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri) by 15 June 2026, document evaluation by the Coordinator, then a study visa. Because the course is open access, that non-EU pre-enrolment window closes and does not reopen: "After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only." CRITICAL WARNING: "Be aware that pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes. In order to matriculate you also need to take and pass the verifications of the entry requirements and the admission procedures set for the degree programme of your interest." And: "Important! The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa." FOREIGN STUDENTS CANNOT SELF-ENROL ONLINE: the University's 2026/2027 enrolment notice states "Gli studenti stranieri per immatricolarsi devono invece contattare via mail le segreterie studenti" - foreign students must instead contact the student office by e-mail to matriculate (for this degree: segreing@unina.it). [uncertain] NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ADMISSION PAGE FOR INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS EXISTS. This degree publishes no annual one-page "admission rules" sheet in English, no application form for foreign qualifications, no evaluation timetable and no published decision deadlines. Everything international is handled through the generic University channels plus direct e-mail to the Coordinator and the two named foreign-enrolment contacts.
academic_requirements: BASELINE: "Per l'iscrizione ad un corso di Laurea Magistrale e necessario essere in possesso di una Laurea o un diploma universitario di durata triennale, o altro titolo acquisito all'estero e riconosciuto idoneo" - a bachelor degree, a three-year university diploma, or another qualification obtained abroad and recognised as suitable. TWO ALTERNATIVE CURRICULAR ROUTES (Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations, reproduced verbatim on the departmental orientation page). ROUTE A - AUTOMATIC: hold a bachelor degree in the class of INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING - "classe 10 del D.M. 509/99 ed L-9 del D.M. 270/04" - or an equivalent qualification. ROUTE B - CREDIT COUNT: have acquired AT LEAST 90 CFU in specified scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD), structured as follows. BLOCK 1 - AT LEAST 40 CFU across these sectors: MATH-02/A (ex MAT/02) Algebra; MATH-02/B (ex MAT/03) Geometria; MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05) Analisi Matematica; MATH-03/B (ex MAT/06) Probabilita e Statistica Matematica; MATH-04/A (ex MAT/07) Fisica Matematica; MATH-05/A (ex MAT/08) Analisi Numerica; MATH-06/A (ex MAT/09) Ricerca Operativa; STAT-01/A (ex SECS-S/01) Statistica; STAT-01/B (ex SECS-S/02) Statistica per la Ricerca Sperimentale e Tecnologica; IINF-05/A (ex ING-INF/05) Sistemi di Elaborazione delle Informazioni; PHYS-01/A Fisica Sperimentale delle Interazioni Fondamentali e Applicazioni; PHYS-03/A Fisica Sperimentale della Materia e Applicazioni; PHYS-04/A Fisica Teorica della Materia, Modelli, Metodi Matematici e Applicazioni; CHEM-03/A (ex CHIM/03) Chimica Generale e Inorganica; CHEM-04/A (ex CHIM/04) Chimica Industriale; CHEM-06/A (ex CHIM/07) Fondamenti Chimici delle Tecnologie. In plain terms: 40 CFU of mathematics, statistics, computer science, physics and chemistry. THIS 18-CFU CORE IS THE MOST LIKELY POINT OF FAILURE FOR A FOREIGN APPLICANT: an applicant with a general mechanical engineering bachelor may have plenty of thermodynamics and turbomachinery, but must be able to document 18 CFU/ECTS of it in fluid machinery, energy systems and applied industrial thermodynamics specifically. TWO SAFETY VALVES FOR THE 18-CFU CORE, both verbatim from Art. 5: (a) equivalence recognition - "la Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico del Corso di Studio puo individuare eventuali equivalenze di crediti di settori scientifico disciplinari differenti da quelli suindicati sulla base dei contenuti di specifici insegnamenti presenti nella carriera pregressa dello studente e strettamente attinenti alle tematiche dei settori suindicati" (the committee may recognise credits from other SSDs based on actual course content, documented through official transcripts); (b) alignment path - L-9 holders with fewer than 18 CFU in those sectors are admitted anyway, with a recommended Individual Study Plan containing an alignment path and no increase in total CFU. WHO CHECKS: "L'accertamento dei requisiti curriculari e effettuato dalla CCD mediante analisi della carriera pregressa dello studente" - the Teaching Coordination Committee assesses the applicant's full prior academic record. IF THE REQUIREMENTS ARE NOT MET: enrolment is refused, and the committee prescribes single course units (Corsi Singoli) whose examinations must be passed BEFORE matriculation - "da effettuarsi anteriormente alla immatricolazione". Note that Corsi Singoli fees are separately payable (and, under the 2026/27 enrolment guide, refundable if the master's enrolment is subsequently completed within the stated term). [uncertain] HOW A FOREIGN DEGREE IS MAPPED ONTO THIS SCHEME IS NOWHERE PUBLISHED. Nothing states how non-Italian ECTS are matched to Italian SSD codes, whether a 3-year 180-ECTS bachelor is required (4-year bachelors are common outside the EU), what evidence of course content is accepted, how long the evaluation takes, or whether a written eligibility decision is issued before the visa stage. The only stated channel is to e-mail the academic transcript and syllabi to the Coordinator (fabio.bozza@unina.it) or to the two foreign-enrolment contacts (francesco.pelella@unina.it, enrica.malfi@unina.it) - do this MONTHS before the 15 June Universitaly deadline. NOTE ON WORDING IN THE CENTRAL RECORD: the central unina.it page still carries a legacy sentence referring to "il corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria per l'Energia e l'Ambiente" (dropping "Meccanica") and requires "la documentata capacita di utilizzare correttamente, in forma scritta e orale, almeno una lingua dell'Unione Europea oltre l'italiano" - documented ability to use at least one EU language besides Italian, in writing and orally.
entry_exam_or_test: THERE IS NO COMPETITIVE ENTRANCE EXAM, BUT THERE IS A CONDITIONAL ADMISSION TEST. Sequence: curricular requirements are checked first; only applicants who hold them proceed to the personal-preparation check; that check is passed AUTOMATICALLY on a grade average, and only those below the threshold sit a test. THE AUTOMATIC PASS, verbatim: "A tal fine si considera la media M pesata sulla base delle consistenze in CFU, delle votazioni (in trentesimi), conseguite negli esami di profitto necessari per il conseguimento del titolo di Laurea che da accesso al Corso di Laurea Magistrale. La personale preparazione dello studente si ritiene adeguata se M >= 24." English version: "the weighted average grade M based on the CFU credits of the courses and the marks (on 30-point scale) obtained in the exams required for the Bachelor's Degree, granting access to the Master's Programme, is computed. Academic preparation is considered adequate if M >= 24." So a CFU-weighted bachelor examination average of at least 24/30 clears the gate with no test. (24/30 is roughly 80% on the Italian scale; broadly comparable to a UK 2:1, a US GPA around 3.0-3.2, or an ECTS C/B boundary - but no official conversion table is published for this course.) THE ADMISSION TEST for everyone below 24/30: "Gli studenti che non soddisfano il precedente criterio dovranno sostenere uno specifico Test di ammissione." FORMAT: 35 multiple-choice questions drawn at random from a published bank of 140. COVERAGE: 5 questions randomly drawn from 20 available for EACH of ten mechanical-engineering sectors - IIND-06/A Macchine a Fluido; IIND-06/B Sistemi per l'Energia e l'Ambiente; IIND-07/A Fisica Tecnica Industriale; IIND-07/B Fisica Tecnica Ambientale; IMIS-01/A Misure Meccaniche e Termiche; IIND-02/A Meccanica Applicata alle Macchine; IIND-03/A Progettazione Meccanica e Costruzione di Macchine; IIND-03/B Disegno e Metodi dell'Ingegneria Industriale; IIND-04/A Tecnologie e Sistemi di Lavorazione; IIND-05/A Impianti Industriali Meccanici. PASS MARK: "Il Test si intendera superato se lo studente avra risposto positivamente a 21 dei 35 quesiti" - 21 correct out of 35 (60%). THE FULL QUESTION BANK IS PUBLISHED IN ADVANCE - all 140 questions: http://meccanica.dii.unina.it/images/lmpp/Lista_domande_Test.pdf. Note the URL path is /lmpp/ because the same bank and the same test serve BOTH LM-33 master's degrees (Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente and Ingegneria Meccanica per la Progettazione e la Produzione). RETAKE RULES: "Il Test puo essere ripetuto al massimo tre volte con intervallo minimo di un mese tra due prove successive" - a maximum of three attempts, minimum one month apart; and "qualora lo studente dosse sostenere con esito negativo il test in una delle date su riportate, non potra partecipare alla prova nella data immediatamente successiva" - after a failure you must skip the very next scheduled date. SITTINGS SCHEDULED UP TO DECEMBER 2026 (published on the departmental orientation page): 20 January 2026; 24 February 2026; 7 April 2026; 22 June 2026; 21 July 2026; 13 OCTOBER 2026; 10 NOVEMBER 2026; 22 DECEMBER 2026. The last three are still ahead as of 30 August 2026. BOOKING: a Microsoft Forms booking link published on the same page - https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=auLPL2K7sEax4yj52gxF_SXeNKE0iP1Iolr3mbJyvztUMDZRWDFIQVRHSzVMQVdQVEJWUUdHMVAxQy4u . The page also warns "Seguiranno ulteriori comunicazioni circa le modalita e lo svolgimento della prova" - further communications about the format and conduct of the test will follow. EXAMINING COMMITTEE: President Prof. Luca Esposito; commissioners Ing. Luca Boccarusso and Ing. Luca Viscito. SELF-ASSESSMENT IS RECOMMENDED FOR EVERYONE: the programme advises all incoming students, whatever their bachelor average, to take the self-assessment test anyway, "soprattutto con riferimento ai quesiti inerenti alla Fisica Tecnica e alle Macchine, che costituiscono le aree di apprendimento caratterizzanti" - especially the Applied Thermodynamics and Machines questions, the programme's characterising learning areas. Students may also sit it BEFORE graduating, purely to gauge their preparation. Applicants are additionally told to read the course descriptions (Schede degli Insegnamenti) with their syllabi and prerequisites at https://www.corsi.unina.it/D20/docenti/2025. THERE IS ALSO A LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY TEST - see language_requirements. It is part of the same compulsory "verification of personal preparation" and applies only to those without a degree taught in Italian or English and without a B1 certificate in either language. NO TOLC, NO GRE/GMAT, NO PORTFOLIO, NO INTERVIEW is required or mentioned anywhere for this degree. [uncertain] THE TEST'S APPLICABILITY TO FOREIGN-DEGREE APPLICANTS IS UNRESOLVED. The rule is written around a CFU-weighted Italian 30-point average, which cannot be computed directly from most foreign transcripts. Nothing published states whether the CCD converts foreign grades, deems the average unavailable and therefore requires the test, or waives it. Nor is it stated whether the test can be sat remotely from abroad - the booking form and the phrase "somministrato da una apposita commissione" suggest a supervised sitting, and the sittings are on fixed dates, most of which fall AFTER the 15 June Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline. An applicant below 24/30 should raise this explicitly with Prof. Bozza and Prof. Esposito before pre-enrolling.
seats_total: NO SEAT LIMIT IS SET - the programme is open access (accesso libero con verifica di preparazione), so no total number of places exists to be published. EVIDENCE: (1) the orientation-portal fact sheet records the admission mode as "Verifica di preparazione", not "numero programmato"; (2) the University's official 2026/2027 index of programmed-number courses lists only five two-year master's degrees - Precision Livestock Farming, Professioni sanitarie, Psicologia Clinica e degli interventi nei contesti sociali e dello sviluppo, Scienze Enologiche, Scienze della Nutrizione Umana - and this degree is not among them; (3) no bando, no ranking (graduatoria), no application fee and no application deadline of a competitive kind is published for it anywhere on unina.it; (4) Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations mentions "l'eventuale programmazione delle iscrizioni" only as a power the CCD could exercise in future, footnoting Law 264/1999 - it has not been exercised. PRACTICAL MEANING: anyone who satisfies the curricular requirements and clears the personal-preparation gate can enrol; there is no competition against other candidates. [uncertain] NO COHORT SIZE IS PUBLISHED FOR THE PROGRAMME OR FOR THE SUSTAINABLE ENERGY CURRICULUM. Neither the orientation portal nor the departmental site nor the Didactic Regulations state how many students enrol per year in LM-IMEA as a whole, how many choose the English SE path, or whether the SE path is activated only above a minimum cohort. AlmaLaurea's transparency record (codicione 0630107303400002) carries graduate statistics, but was not used here as it is a third-party aggregator rather than a unina.it source and the research brief restricts sources to unina.it. If cohort size matters to the decision, ask Prof. Bozza or Prof. Mauro directly.
non_eu_reserved_seats: NO RESERVED NON-EU QUOTA IS PUBLISHED, AND NONE IS EXPECTED, BECAUSE THE COURSE IS OPEN ACCESS. Reserved non-EU contingents at Federico II are declared inside the bando of each numero-programmato course (for example the bachelor bandi published for 2026/27 declare a specific number of places for non-EU candidates residing abroad, sometimes with a sub-quota for citizens of China under the Marco Polo programme). This degree publishes no bando at all, so there is no quota table, no sub-quota and no ranking for non-EU applicants. WHAT REPLACES THE QUOTA for a non-EU applicant residing abroad: an individual document evaluation by the Programme Coordinator, following compulsory pre-enrolment on the Universitaly portal by 15 June 2026, then a study visa. International.unina.it states the principle for the other direction too: "Non-European candidates, wherever they reside and regularly residing in Italy or in a European Union country, have unrestricted access to university courses if they hold a qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification" - non-EU citizens already legally resident in Italy or the EU bypass Universitaly entirely and go straight to the Coordinator. [uncertain] THE ABSENCE OF A PUBLISHED QUOTA IS INFERRED, NOT STATED. No unina.it page says in words "there is no reserved quota for non-EU students on this degree"; the conclusion rests on the course's absence from the numero-programmato index and on the general open-access rule. Federico II does file per-course non-EU availability figures with the Universitaly portal each year, and that filing was not accessible from unina.it sources (the University's own UniversItaly information sheet, https://www.unina.it/documents/20117/4260320/UniversItaly_2026_27.pdf, is a scanned image whose text could not be extracted). A non-EU applicant should confirm availability with the Coordinator before the June deadline.
language_requirements: THIS IS THE MOST COUNTER-INTUITIVE FIELD IN THIS RECORD, SO READ IT IN FULL: DESPITE HOSTING A FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT CURRICULUM, THE DEGREE DOES NOT REQUIRE AN ENGLISH CERTIFICATE TO BE ADMITTED. There is no IELTS/TOEFL threshold, no B2 English entry requirement, and no English-language interview in the admission rules. THE ACTUAL ENTRY RULE, verbatim from Art. 5: "Per quanto attiene invece alla verifica di adeguate competenze linguistiche, le studentesse e gli studenti non in possesso di un titolo di studio ottenuto a seguito della frequenza di un corso di studio erogato in lingua italiana o inglese, e non in possesso di certificazioni o idoneita linguistiche relative alla conoscenza della lingua italiana o inglese almeno a livello B1 del Quadro Comune Europeo di Riferimento (QCER), dovranno dimostrare, in un test di idoneita, di possedere adeguate capacita di comprensione e conversazione in italiano o in inglese." Official English rendering: "students who have not obtained a degree taught in Italian or English, and who do not possess a certification or attestation of language proficiency in either language at a minimum B1 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), are required to demonstrate adequate comprehension and conversational skills in Italian or English through a proficiency test." UNPACKING THAT RULE: (a) the bar is B1, not B2; (b) it is satisfied by ITALIAN **OR** ENGLISH - Italian alone formally satisfies it, even for someone intending to follow the English curriculum; (c) it is waived outright if your bachelor was taught in Italian or English (so a graduate of any English-medium university needs no certificate at all); (d) only if you have neither a qualifying degree nor a B1 certificate do you sit a spoken/comprehension proficiency test. This is a low bar by international standards - do not confuse it with the B2 entry requirements common at northern-Italian universities. THE B2 ENGLISH REQUIREMENT IS A GRADUATION REQUIREMENT, NOT AN ADMISSION ONE. Every study plan carries 3 CFU of "Ulteriori Conoscenze Linguistiche" / "Additional Language Proficiency" (TAF F). Verbatim note (e): "studenti non in possesso della certificazione di conoscenza della Lingua Inglese, almeno a livello B2 del Quadro Comune Europeo di Riferimento (QCER), hanno l'obbligo di prevedere nel piano di studi un numero di CFU per le Ulteriori Conoscenze Linguistiche adeguato a garantire il raggiungimento di tale livello di conoscenza (3 CFU). Tali crediti sono acquisibili presso enti esterni o presso il centro linguistico di ateneo (cla.unina.it) e sono riconosciuti all'atto della presentazione della certificazione. Studenti che all'atto dell'immatricolazione siano gia in possesso di attestato di inglese almeno di livello B2 ne richiedono il riconoscimento ai fini delle Ulteriori Conoscenze Linguistiche (3 CFU)." So: arrive with a B2 English certificate and you get the 3 CFU recognised for free; arrive without one and you must reach B2 through the University Language Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, cla.unina.it) or an external body before you can graduate. The departmental orientation page confirms "B2 e un requisito obbligatorio per la laurea" (B2 is a mandatory requirement for graduation). FOR NON-MINOR STUDENTS the 3 CFU may alternatively be earned through University-approved MOOCs on the "Federica Web Learning" platform or participation in University student initiatives; for Minor-in-Green-Technologies students they are earned by attending accredited seminars. NO ITALIAN LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT FOR AN ENGLISH-TAUGHT PATH. International.unina.it: "If you choose a three-year degree course, magistral degree course or single-cycle magistral degree course in ITALIAN, a B2 level Italian language proficiency is required" (CLIQ-system certificates: Universita per Stranieri di Perugia, Universita per Stranieri di Siena, Roma Tre, Societa Dante Alighieri, Universita per Stranieri Dante Alighieri di Reggio Calabria), whereas "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required." It adds a practical note for the visa: "Remember that an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation." BOTTOM LINE FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: bring a B2+ English certificate anyway. It is not needed for admission, but it (i) satisfies the B1 entry gate outright, (ii) is explicitly useful at the visa interview, (iii) is recognised immediately as the 3 graduation CFU, and (iv) is the only realistic evidence that you can follow a curriculum taught wholly in English. [uncertain] THREE GAPS. (1) No unina.it page states the ENGLISH level actually needed to cope with the Sustainable Energy curriculum, nor whether the Coordinator applies an informal English screen when evaluating foreign applicants for the SE path - the written rule would let an Italian-B1 applicant enrol on an all-English curriculum, which is clearly not the intent. (2) The format, scheduling and location of the "test di idoneita" language proficiency test are not published: no dates, no sample, no remote-sitting statement. (3) The central unina.it record adds a legacy requirement of "documentata capacita di utilizzare correttamente, in forma scritta e orale, almeno una lingua dell'Unione Europea oltre l'italiano", which is phrased for Italian-speaking students and is not reconciled anywhere with the B1 Italian-or-English rule. Ask Prof. Mauro (alfonsowilliam.mauro@unina.it) for the current practice.
application_deadline_eu: THERE IS NO COMPETITIVE APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR EU/EU-TREATED APPLICANTS, BECAUSE THERE IS NO SELECTION. What exists are (a) the University's enrolment (immatricolazione) window, (b) the admission-test sittings for those below 24/30, and (c) the study-plan deadline at which the English curriculum is chosen. ENROLMENT WINDOW FOR a.y. 2026/2027 (binding source: "Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27", section "Date importanti da ricordare"): 16 JULY 2026 - "Inizio periodo ordinario immatricolazione" (ordinary matriculation period opens; matriculation = first-time enrolment on a bachelor, master's or single-cycle degree). 1 SEPTEMBER 2026 - ordinary period opens for transfers and course changes. 2 NOVEMBER 2026 - "Scadenza periodo ordinario immatricolazione e iscrizione agli anni successivi" (ordinary matriculation deadline), also the deadline for the direct INPS retrieval of ISEEU income data. 3 NOVEMBER 2026 - extraordinary period opens. 15 JANUARY 2027 - last day to matriculate late with a EUR 50 surcharge. 16 JANUARY 2027 - late matriculation continues with a EUR 110 surcharge. CONFLICTING DATE ON THE UNIVERSITY'S OWN PAGES - see uncertainty_notes: the orientation portal's 2026/2027 enrolment notice (published 14 July 2026) says "e possibile procedere all'immatricolazione a partire dal 16 luglio e fino al 31 ottobre 2026" (until 31 October 2026), whereas the binding Guida gives 2 November 2026. 31 October 2026 is a Saturday and 2 November the following Monday, which most likely explains the difference; treat 31 October 2026 as the safe date. THE PROGRAMME'S OWN STATEMENT (orientation portal, "Application timeline"): "Enrolment at 1st and subsequent years usually take place from September, 1st to October 31st of each year, in accordance with procedures that are announced in a specific Guide to enrolment and payment of fees published at the URL: https://www.unina.it/didattica/sportello-studenti/guide-dello-studente". This programme-page text is a year-generic summary and is superseded by the 2026/27 Guida for the actual dates. FIRST INSTALMENT TIMING: the first instalment (60% of the contribution + regional tax + stamp duty) is payable "Dal 16 luglio (immatricolazioni L o iscrizioni I anno LM) o dall'1 settembre ed entro il 2 novembre 2026" - i.e. first-year master's enrolments can pay from 16 July, and in all cases by 2 November 2026. ADMISSION-TEST SITTINGS STILL OPEN in the current cycle (only relevant if your bachelor average is below 24/30): 13 October 2026, 10 November 2026, 22 December 2026. Book through the Microsoft Forms link on http://meccanica.dii.unina.it/it/orientamento-lmea. Because a failed sitting bars you from the immediately following date, leaving the test to October is risky against a 2 November enrolment deadline. STUDY-PLAN DEADLINE - THE DATE THAT ACTUALLY SELECTS THE ENGLISH CURRICULUM: "The Study Plan is normally submitted by October 31st of each academic year" (orientation portal). The student communicates the chosen path (SEI, GAE, SP or SE) to the Engineering Student Office; instructions at http://meccanica.dii.unina.it/it/piani-di-studio-lmea. Miss this and you have not formally chosen the Sustainable Energy path. EU CITIZENS AND EU-RESIDENT APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION have no portal deadline at all - they send documents to the Coordinator whenever they are ready, but must leave the Coordinator enough time to assess eligibility before the enrolment window closes. Note also that foreign-qualification holders cannot use SegrePass and must enrol by e-mailing segreing@unina.it. [uncertain] NO PROGRAMME-LEVEL EVALUATION CALENDAR EXISTS. There is no published date by which the Coordinator must respond to a document submission, no stated evaluation turnaround, and no formal offer letter. The dates above are all University-level; the only programme-specific dates in the whole record are the admission-test sittings and the 31 October study-plan deadline. Dates for a.y. 2027/2028 were not published as of 30 August 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu: THE ONLY HARD DEADLINE IN THIS ENTIRE RECORD, AND IT IS EARLY: 15 JUNE 2026 for Universitaly pre-enrolment for a.y. 2026/2027. Verbatim from international.unina.it: "JUNE - 15 - 2026 - Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only." READ THE LAST SENTENCE CAREFULLY: because this degree is OPEN ACCESS (not restricted access), its non-EU pre-enrolment window closes on 15 June and does NOT reopen. AS OF 30 AUGUST 2026 THIS DEADLINE HAS PASSED for the 2026/2027 intake - a non-EU applicant residing abroad is now targeting a.y. 2027/2028, whose deadline had not been published at the time of research but has fallen in mid-June in recent cycles. SECOND DEADLINE: "NOVEMBER - 30 - 2026 - Deadline for submitting the Visa Application at Italian Embassies/Consulates." THE PROCEDURE, in the University's own words. "The university pre-enrolment application is the first step to be taken by a candidate in order to apply for a visa for study purposes at an Italian diplomatic representation." "University pre-enrolment is a compulsory procedure, which is the responsibility of the Embassy and precedes the phase of issuing the study visa and the university enrolment phases; it concerns foreign students abroad and must be concluded before the student's enrolment procedure at the chosen university." "The pre-enrolment application is made exclusively through the Universitaly portal (visit https://www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri)." In the application you indicate the University of Naples Federico II, choose the degree programme, and specify the Embassy/Consulate where you will apply for the visa. TWO WARNINGS THE UNIVERSITY PRINTS IN BOLD. "Be aware that pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes. In order to matriculate you also need to take and pass the verifications of the entry requirements and the admission procedures set for the degree programme of your interest." And: "Important! The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa." So there is no admission letter to wait for - the validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary is what you take to the Embassy. WHAT THE EMBASSY NEEDS FROM YOU: "the summary of the pre-enrolment application submitted through Universitaly and validated by the University of Naples Federico II; any language competence certificates; the documents required for the visa application, including a health insurance policy where applicable; the required documents if you hold a foreign qualification." WHAT YOU GET BACK: a type "D" study visa ("studio - immatricolazione universita"), a stamped health insurance policy where applicable, and your returned qualification documents. VISA FINANCIAL AND MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS, verbatim: "Economic means of subsistence for the planned stay equal to EUR 10.179,85 per year, proven by means of personal financial guarantees or those of parents or Italian or foreign citizens legally residing in Italian territory, or provided by Italian institutions and bodies of proven credit"; funds for repatriation (a return ticket suffices); suitable accommodation in Italy; adequate medical/hospitalisation insurance cover. If the University confirms your pre-enrolment "with reservations" (qualification not yet in hand, or admission/language check still pending), the consulate still issues the type D visa so you can sit the checks in Italy without returning home. AFTER ARRIVAL: apply for the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) - a EUR 16 duty stamp, EUR 30.46 + EUR 40.00 permit fee and about EUR 30 registered-post charge at the Post Office, plus the enrolment certificate from segreing@unina.it sent to the Questura. NON-EU CITIZENS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU ARE EXEMPT FROM ALL OF THIS: "If you are a non-European student without the need for a visa and regularly residing in Italy with a regular study visa, you may present your academic documents directly to the Coordinator of the Course in which you wish to enrol. You will therefore not need to pre-register on the Universitaly Portal." They then follow the ordinary enrolment window (16 July - 2 November 2026 for 2026/27). [uncertain] FOUR UNRESOLVED POINTS. (1) The 2027/2028 pre-enrolment deadline was not published as of 30 August 2026. required_documents: NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DOCUMENT LIST IS PUBLISHED FOR THIS DEGREE. What follows is the University-wide list from international.unina.it plus the programme-specific evidence implied by the curricular requirements. SET 1 - FOR THE EVALUATION OF A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION (sent to the Coordinator; identical list given for EU candidates and for non-EU candidates resident in Italy/EU), verbatim: "eventual translations; legalisations; Diploma Supplement; certificates of examinations; certificates from the Italian ENIC NARIC centre (CIMEA) https://www.cimea.it/EN/; any declarations of value issued by the competent diplomatic representations". Send these to Prof. Fabio Bozza (fabio.bozza@unina.it) and/or the named foreign-enrolment contacts Prof. Francesco Pelella (francesco.pelella@unina.it) and Prof.ssa Enrica Malfi (enrica.malfi@unina.it). SET 2 - FOR ENROLMENT (matriculation), verbatim from international.unina.it "Documents required for enrolment": "Copy of passport; Application form; 1 passport photo; Tax code [codice fiscale]; Residence permit (proof of having applied for it); Declaration of value issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained or certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC centres." The page adds: "Important: always check the instructions on the degree programme's website." The secretariat (segreing@unina.it) issues the fee payment form and the enrolment form. SET 3 - FOR THE VISA (non-EU residing abroad): the validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; language competence certificates; health insurance; proof of means of subsistence (EUR 10,179.85/year); proof of accommodation; return-ticket or repatriation funds; the foreign qualification documents. SET 4 - WHAT THE ADMISSION RULES ACTUALLY REQUIRE YOU TO PROVE, even though no form asks for it explicitly: (a) that your bachelor is in the Italian industrial-engineering class L-9 or equivalent, OR a transcript showing at least 90 CFU/ECTS mapped to the listed SSD blocks (>=40 in maths/physics/chemistry/informatics, >=50 in the engineering sectors, of which >=18 in fluid machinery, energy systems and industrial applied thermodynamics); (b) the CFU-weighted average of your bachelor examinations, to establish whether M >= 24/30 (this is what decides whether you sit the admission test); (c) either a degree taught in Italian or English, or a B1+ Italian/English certificate, to clear the language gate. Because the 18-CFU core is judged "sulla base dei contenuti di specifici insegnamenti" (on the content of specific courses), SYLLABI / COURSE DESCRIPTIONS for your thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid machinery and energy-systems courses are in practice essential even though no list names them. USEFUL EXTRAS, not formally required: a B2+ English certificate (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge - explicitly "useful for the issue of the visa", and recognised as the 3 graduation CFU); a CV; and, if you intend to take the Minor in Green Technologies, nothing extra at admission (the Minor is chosen later, via the study plan). [uncertain] SIGNIFICANT GAPS. There is no downloadable application form for foreign-qualification holders on the programme site; no stated rule on whether a CIMEA Statement of Comparability is accepted in place of a Declaration of Value (the University lists both as alternatives, but consulates differ); no stated translation/legalisation standard (sworn translation? apostille?); no stated deadline for submitting documents to the Coordinator; and no confirmation of whether digital copies suffice for the initial evaluation. Confirm the exact package by e-mail with segreing@unina.it and the Coordinator before travelling.
tuition_or_fees_link: OFFICIAL LINKS: University enrolment-and-fees hub https://www.unina.it/didattica/sportello-studenti/guide-dello-studente (the link the programme's own "Application timeline" section points to) | fees section https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse | the binding 2026/27 document "Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27" https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 | official fee simulator http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ | international-student summary https://www.international.unina.it/education/admission-regulation/ | enrolment portal https://www.segrepass.unina.it . The programme's own website publishes NO fee page of its own. SHORT ANSWER FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: this degree is close to free. Non-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus a EUR 16 stamp; EU non-Italian citizens pay a flat EUR 200 contribution plus the regional tax and stamp. Realistic 2026/27 totals: roughly EUR 167 per year for a non-EU student and roughly EUR 367 per year for an EU non-Italian student (using the EUR 151 band that the Guida assigns to households resident abroad). THE BINDING RULES (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27, "Esoneri parziali"): "stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio secondo le disposizioni di cui al punto 1 sopra e l'imposta di bollo, entro il termine ordinario di scadenza per il versamento della I rata"; "europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR. Se inferiore, possono effettuare l'iscrizione nella modalita ordinaria." Foreign holders of an annual Italian Government scholarship under development-cooperation or intergovernmental cultural/scientific agreements are also totally exempt from the contribution. For Italian students the ISEEU system applies instead, with a reduced first-year "contributo agevolato". REGIONAL RIGHT-TO-STUDY TAX BANDS 2026/27 (D.M. n. 176 of 24 February 2026), verbatim: EUR 130.00 for ISEEU up to and including EUR 25,500 and for students from particularly poor countries under art. 13 c. 5 DPCM 9 April 2001; EUR 151.00 for ISEEU between EUR 25,500.01 and EUR 51,000 AND for students whose household resides abroad; EUR 173.00 for ISEEU above EUR 51,000 or where no ISEEU declaration is filed. Stamp duty (imposta di bollo) EUR 16.00. BUDGET EUR 151 IF YOUR FAMILY LIVES ABROAD - that is the band the Guida assigns explicitly to internationally resident households. INSTALMENTS 2026/27: 1st instalment = 60% of the contribution + regional tax + stamp, payable from 16 July (for first-year master's enrolments) or from 1 September, and in any case by 2 November 2026; 2nd instalment = 20%, by 1 March 2027; 3rd instalment = 20%, by 30 April 2027; a EUR 100 surcharge applies from 16 July 2027 to anyone who has not paid the 2nd or 3rd instalment. Late enrolment surcharges: EUR 50 up to 15 January 2027, EUR 110 from 16 January 2027. Amounts paid are refundable only where an exemption applies; withdrawal from studies produces no refund. OTHER COSTS TO BUDGET: residence permit for non-EU students (EUR 16 duty stamp + EUR 30.46 + EUR 40.00 permit fee + about EUR 30 registered post); proof of means of subsistence for the visa (EUR 10,179.85/year, a requirement, not a fee); Corsi Singoli fees if the CCD prescribes missing curricular credits before matriculation. There is NO application fee and NO admission-test fee for this degree. FUNDING: no programme-specific scholarship scheme is published. Regional right-to-study grants come from ADISURC; Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs fellowships are available to applicants from eligible countries (https://studyinitaly.esteri.it/en/home_borse). A refund of up to 10% of the last year's fees exists for students who graduate within the normal duration, allocated by ranking within each teaching area. [uncertain] TWO DIFFERENT REGIONAL-TAX FIGURES ARE PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT AND THEY DO NOT AGREE. international.unina.it states "European students EUR 200/year (tuition fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory) - Non-european students EUR 140/year regional fee (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)", i.e. a flat EUR 140, whereas the binding 2026/27 Guida gives the banded EUR 130 / 151 / 173. USE THE GUIDA; the EUR 140 figure on the international pages appears to be a stale carry-over. The tuition components themselves (EUR 200 for EU citizens, total exemption for non-EU citizens) are consistent across sources and are not in doubt.

uncertainty_notes: 1. THE BRIEF'S PROGRAMME NAME IS WRONG AND THIS MATTERS OPERATIONALLY. The research brief describes an English curriculum called "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment". No such curriculum exists. "Mechanical Engineering for Energy and the Environment" is the English rendering of the whole Italian degree "Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente" (LM-33), which is bilingual (ENG/ITA). The English-taught curriculum inside it is "SUSTAINABLE ENERGY" (Italian: "Energia Sostenibile"), acronym SE. Any listing, e-mail or application should name the Sustainable Energy curriculum explicitly. 2. THE DIPLOMA CARRIES THE ITALIAN DEGREE NAME ONLY. The qualification awarded is "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica per l'Energia e l'Ambiente", class LM-33. The curriculum (Sustainable Energy) is a study-plan choice, not part of the degree title, and does not appear in the legal name of the qualification. This is exactly the case the research brief anticipated. 3. THREE OF THE FOUR CURRICULA HAVE ENGLISH-LOOKING NAMES BUT ARE TAUGHT IN ITALIAN. "Innovative Energy Systems", "Advanced Energy Management" and "Propulsion Systems" are English translations of Sistemi Energetici Innovativi, Gestione Avanzata dell'Energia and Sistemi Propulsivi, all Italian-taught. The English-language departmental page https://meccanica.dii.unina.it/en/info-lmea-en lists all five paths with English names and gives no language marker, which is actively misleading. Only the Didactic Regulations' "CURRICULA AND LANGUAGES" table and the orientation portal's "study plan in detail" section state the languages correctly. 4. THE CURRICULUM IS CHOSEN AFTER ENROLMENT, NOT AT ADMISSION. There is no separate application, seat allocation or admission route for the English path. A student enrols in LM-IMEA and then declares SE when submitting the Study Plan, normally by 31 October. Nothing published guarantees the SE path runs in a given year or states a minimum cohort. 5. NO ENGLISH CERTIFICATE IS REQUIRED TO BE ADMITTED TO AN ALL-ENGLISH CURRICULUM. The entry language gate is B1 in ITALIAN **OR** ENGLISH, and is waived entirely for anyone whose bachelor was taught in Italian or English. B2 English is a GRADUATION requirement (3 CFU), not an entry one. This is a genuine rule, quoted verbatim, but it is so unusual that applicants should verify current practice with Prof. Alfonso William Mauro before relying on it. The format, dates and location of the fallback "test di idoneita" language test are not published anywhere. 6. FOREIGN-DEGREE MAPPING IS THE BIGGEST PRACTICAL UNKNOWN. The curricular requirement is written in Italian SSD codes (>=90 CFU, with >=40 in maths/physics/chemistry/informatics, >=50 in engineering sectors, of which >=18 in IIND-06/A + IIND-06/B + IIND-07/A). No unina.it page explains how foreign ECTS are mapped to those codes, whether a 180-ECTS three-year bachelor is required, what syllabus evidence is accepted, how long evaluation takes, or whether a written eligibility decision is issued. The only channel is direct e-mail to the Coordinator (fabio.bozza@unina.it) or the two named foreign-enrolment contacts (francesco.pelella@unina.it, enrica.malfi@unina.it). 7. THE 24/30 AVERAGE RULE CANNOT BE APPLIED MECHANICALLY TO A FOREIGN TRANSCRIPT. The rule assumes a CFU-weighted Italian 30-point average. Nothing states whether the CCD converts foreign grades, treats the average as unavailable and therefore requires the 35-question admission test, or waives the test. It is also not stated whether the test can be sat remotely from abroad. Most remaining 2026 sittings (13 October, 10 November, 22 December 2026) fall after both the 15 June Universitaly deadline and, for two of them, the 30 November visa deadline - a sequencing problem the University does not address. 8. THE NON-EU DEADLINE FOR THE CURRENT CYCLE HAS PASSED. 15 June 2026 was the Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline for a.y. 2026/2027, and because the course is open access it did not reopen ("After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only"). As of 30 August 2026 a non-EU applicant residing abroad is targeting a.y. 2027/2028, whose deadline was not yet published. There is also no published service standard for how quickly Federico II validates a Universitaly pre-enrolment - and without validation the Embassy will not issue the visa. 9.
